title: Safety from exponential matrix control barrier functions
author: Pio Ong, Yicheng Xu, Ryan M. Bena, Faryar Jabbari, Aaron D. Ames
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 1 (source label thm:EMCBF-safety), the safety theorem of the matrix control barrier function framework: if H is an exponential MCBF then the safe set defined by the matrix inequality H(x) >= 0 is control invariant and the semidefinite-programming safety filter CBF-SDP is continuous on a neighborhood of the safe set. The unit is not a qualification exercise because the counted claim cannot be reached without the whole source-local framework that the unit retains: the matrix-valued barrier condition with its entry-wise Lie derivative matrix and the auxiliary scalarized function argument proving forward invariance (Proposition 1 and its complete proof), the exponential MCBF definition with its strict matrix inequality, and the proof of the counted theorem itself, which constructs the feasible set as a set-valued map, identifies it with a sublevel set of the minimum-eigenvalue function, uses global Lipschitzness of the eigenvalue function on symmetric matrices, and then invokes lower semicontinuity of a convex-valued map with nonempty interior together with the continuity of the minimal selection of a closed convex-valued lower semicontinuous map to obtain continuity of the safety filter before closing the argument with the matrix barrier condition. The retained uncounted Proposition 2 with its own complete proof adds the nonsmooth eigenvalue bound obtained from the generalized gradient through Caratheodory's theorem for convex hulls and the comparison lemma. Combining matrix inequalities and semidefinite programming with set-valued analysis and nonsmooth eigenvalue analysis into a new safety framework is research-level control theory, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
